article.title: Choose One Priority Before Opening Your Inbox
article.why: 練習用簡單英文建立工作優先順序，避免一天從被動回應訊息開始。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Before you open your inbox in the morning, choose one result that would make the day feel useful. It can be small: finish a slide, check a data table, send a proposal, or solve one customer problem. Write it down in one sentence.

This habit matters because an inbox contains other people's priorities. A new message can look urgent even when it is not important. If you start by reading every message, your plan can disappear before you decide what you really need to do. You may spend the morning answering easy questions and leave your most important work for the afternoon, when your energy is lower.

Choosing one priority does not mean ignoring email. It simply gives you a reference point. After you choose the result, you can open your inbox and decide which messages support it, which messages truly need a quick answer, and which can wait. The priority helps you compare requests instead of reacting to each one separately.

The priority should be specific enough to finish. “Work on the report” is vague. “Write the first two pages of the report” is clearer. A clear result makes it easier to start and easier to know when you are done. If the task is too large, choose the next visible step.

Some days will change. A customer problem, system failure, or manager request may become more important than your original plan. That is fine. The goal is not to follow the first plan no matter what. The goal is to begin the day with a choice instead of beginning with automatic reaction.

Try this tomorrow. Before opening email or chat, write one sentence: “Today, the most important result is ___.” Then spend ten or fifteen minutes moving that result forward. Even a short start creates momentum. When messages arrive later, you will know what they are competing with, and your day is less likely to become a list written entirely by other people.
paragraphs.zh: 早上先選出一個最重要的具體成果，再開信箱。信箱裝的是別人的優先事項；先有自己的 reference point，才能判斷哪些訊息真的重要、哪些可以等。優先事項不是死規則，遇到真正緊急狀況仍可調整。
paragraphs.ja: 朝、受信箱を開く前に、その日に達成したい最重要の成果を一つ決めます。受信箱には他人の優先事項が入っているため、自分の基準を先に持つことで、緊急性と重要性を分けやすくなります。状況が変われば優先順位を変えて構いません。

vocabulary.usage: Choose one priority before opening your inbox.
The priority gives you a reference point.
Do not react to every message automatically.
Make the result specific enough to finish.
Messages are competing with your chosen priority.

phrases.example: Spend ten minutes moving the priority forward.

grammar.title: Before + V-ing
grammar.body: Before opening email 表示「在打開郵件之前」；介系詞 before 後可接動名詞。

business.term: What is the most important result today?
business.explanation: 先對齊今日最重要成果
business.example: Before we start, what is the most important result today?

business.term: This can wait until this afternoon.
business.example: This request can wait until this afternoon.

quiz.question: Why can opening the inbox first be risky?
quiz.answer: Because other people's requests can replace your own priorities before you choose them.

quiz.question: Output: Write one specific result for tomorrow.
quiz.answer: Example: Finish the first two slides of the client update.
